set.st: Dr. W. H. Brisbane's serial 'Coon Bluff' (Mineral Point Weekly Tribune, Oct-Dec 1859) tells of a man-made cave dug into Coon Bluff near Arena, on the road to Helena, by a company of white men hunting a golden treasure that an Indian tradition told of; locals believed it a counterfeiters' hideout. The story is fiction, but it shows the belief was local by 1859. In October 1933 (AP, Arena dateline) William and Homer Sweeney of Wyoming drilled and blasted a shaft through the limestone into a sealed chamber 'which originally formed a part of a cave in Coon Rock bluff', after gold in government bars that Indians had told of. By December 1933 they had drilled for two months from the bluff top and were jailed for stealing mill equipment near Linden to keep the dig going; no find was reported. The 1941 WPA Wisconsin guide (Tour 20) also tells the legend. This is Coon Rock near Arena, not the Coon Bluff cliff in Sauk County. Early 1880s: Indian robbers burglarized a Mississippi steamboat purser's safe at Prairie du Chien and said they hid the loot in a cave high in the Coon Rock bluffs near Arena; never recovered. Gard (1962): Coon Rock Cave is 4.5 mi W of Arena on the Hodgson farm.

src: Eau Claire Leader-Telegram, 10 Dec 1933, p. 3 (Dodgeville wire) (Newspapers.com 267192785)
